evaluations.evidence: entering a name and an optional description
evaluations.rationale: Terms are concrete and specific; no phrase allows materially different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: invite estimators by giving them a URL
evaluations.rationale: Clear action and artifact (URL); no ambiguous terminology.

evaluations.evidence: entering an item in a single multi-line text field
evaluations.rationale: Specifies input method unambiguously (single multi-line field).

evaluations.evidence: see all items we try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: Scope (this session) and artifact (items) are clear; wording not materially ambiguous.

evaluations.evidence: select an item to be estimated or re-estimated
evaluations.rationale: Action and intent are specific; terms not open to multiple material interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: add an item to the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Clear operation and target; duplication of 'so that' is stylistic, not semantic ambiguity.

evaluations.evidence: edit an item ... to make it better reflect the team's understanding
evaluations.rationale: 'Better reflect' is subjective but does not introduce materially different feasible interpretations of the feature itself.

evaluations.evidence: delete an item from the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Clear action and effect; no ambiguous terms that change implementation materially.

evaluations.evidence: show all estimates immediately
evaluations.rationale: 'Immediately' is used in context (show even though not all estimators have given their estimate) and is not likely to yield materially different requirement interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: accept the average of all estimates
evaluations.rationale: 'Average' is ambiguous (mean, median, mode, trimmed mean) and can materially change the result accepted.

evaluations.evidence: "estimate" field filled in automatically if all estimators show the same card
evaluations.rationale: Condition and behavior are explicit and leave little room for materially different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: enter the agreed-upon estimate
evaluations.rationale: Phrase expresses a clear user action; 'agreed-upon' denotes outcome of discussion rather than a technical ambiguity.

evaluations.evidence: estimate a story we estimated earlier in the session again
evaluations.rationale: Timeframe and action are explicit; not open to materially different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: import stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Commonly understood action; any format details are implementation but do not make the story semantically ambiguous.

evaluations.evidence: copy/paste stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Clear user action; no vague terms that would cause materially different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: browse through previous games, so that I can find the previous game I'm looking for
evaluations.rationale: Intent and artifact are clear; search/browse modalities are implementation details, not semantic ambiguities.

evaluations.evidence: view a transcript of a game, so that I can see the stories and estimates
evaluations.rationale: Clear object (transcript) and contents (stories and estimates); not open to multiple material meanings.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a HTML file
evaluations.rationale: File format and artifact are explicitly specified; no ambiguous terminology.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a CSV file
evaluations.rationale: Format and intent are clear and not open to materially different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: delete a game, so that stories and estimates for this game are no longer stored
evaluations.rationale: Action and intended effect are explicit; any deeper policy (soft delete) is an implementation decision, not a semantic ambiguity in the story text.

evaluations.evidence: create an account ... by entering my name, email address, a password and a username
evaluations.rationale: Fields required for account creation are explicitly listed and unambiguous.

evaluations.evidence: log in using my account name and password
evaluations.rationale: Login credentials are explicitly named; not open to materially different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: change my account details
evaluations.rationale: High-level intent is clear; while which fields are editable is not listed, this does not introduce multiple material interpretations of the story itself.

evaluations.evidence: delete my account, so that account information and games are no longer stored
evaluations.rationale: Intended effect is explicit; nuances (e.g., shared game data) are implementation/policy details rather than semantic ambiguity.

evaluations.evidence: see dates and times in my local timezone
evaluations.rationale: Desired presentation is explicit; detection/formatting are implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: get a password reminder by email
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous whether the system should send the actual password (insecure) or a password reset link; this leads to materially different implementations.

evaluations.evidence: select whether to have the team estimate with {0, 1/2, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, etc.} or {0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, etc.}
evaluations.rationale: Two estimation scales are explicitly exemplified and tied to named sequences; although 'etc.' is used, the intent (modified Fibonacci vs powers of 2) is clear enough to avoid materially different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: invite up to 15 estimators
evaluations.rationale: Numeric limit is explicit and unambiguous.

evaluations.evidence: join a game by entering my name on the page I received the URL for
evaluations.rationale: Joining mechanism and data required are specific and not open to materially different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: see the item we're estimating
evaluations.rationale: Artifact and intent are clear; no vague terms that change requirements materially.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we will try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: Scope and artifact are explicit; not semantically ambiguous.

evaluations.evidence: immediately see that an estimate has been given by a specific estimator
evaluations.rationale: Purpose and observable feedback are clear; 'immediately' is in context and not likely to imply different material behavior.

evaluations.evidence: be shown all estimates at the same time after all estimators have given their estimate
evaluations.rationale: Condition and result are explicit (after all have estimated), so interpretation is clear.

evaluations.evidence: change my estimate up until the last person selects a card and all are shown
evaluations.rationale: Cutoff condition is explicitly described; not open to materially different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: see each estimator's prior estimates for the story being estimated
evaluations.rationale: Intent and content (prior estimates for this story) are understandable; timeframe implied (prior for this story) is not likely to create materially different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: see who gave what estimates during the current round
evaluations.rationale: Items and scope (current round) are explicit; not ambiguous.

evaluations.evidence: start a two-minute countdown timer that all participants can see
evaluations.rationale: Timer duration and visibility are explicitly stated; functionality is unambiguous.

evaluations.evidence: two-minute timer reset itself as soon as we all play an estimate
evaluations.rationale: Reset trigger and effect are explicitly described; interpretation is clear.

evaluations.evidence: scroll back through the stories and estimates from prior rounds
evaluations.rationale: Action and scope are explicit; not open to materially different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: always have the cards in the same order across multiple draws
evaluations.rationale: Desired invariant (consistent order) is explicit; implementation choices do not change semantic meaning.

evaluations.evidence: change my estimate as long as the draw has not been completed
evaluations.rationale: Condition and action are explicitly stated; not materially ambiguous.

evaluations.evidence: have a small thumbnail photo displayed near where my cards are played
evaluations.rationale: 'Small' is subjective but does not create materially different interpretations of whether a thumbnail should be shown; size details are implementation.

evaluations.evidence: compliant with XHTML and CSS standards
evaluations.rationale: Standards are named explicitly; while versioning could be specified later, the requirement is not semantically vague.

evaluations.evidence: have a list of definitions for commonly used terms
evaluations.rationale: Purpose and artifact are clear; nothing suggests multiple material interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: so that the queries run as fast as possible
evaluations.rationale: 'As fast as possible' is vague and can lead to materially different optimization goals and acceptance criteria.

evaluations.evidence: function correctly in Internet Explorer 6 and 7, Firefox 1.5 and 2, and Safari 2
evaluations.rationale: Browsers and versions are explicitly listed, leaving little room for multiple interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: comply with the W3C accessibility guidelines where possible
evaluations.rationale: 'Where possible' is vague and can be interpreted differently with materially different compliance outcomes.

evaluations.evidence: have the application respond quickly to my actions
evaluations.rationale: Term 'quickly' is underspecified (no measurable threshold) and can lead to materially different expectations.

evaluations.evidence: be able to use Unicode
evaluations.rationale: Requirement is concrete (support Unicode); not open to materially different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: see sensible and predictable URLs
evaluations.rationale: 'Sensible and predictable' are subjective terms that can be interpreted in materially different ways by stakeholders.

evaluations.evidence: have nice error pages when something goes wrong
evaluations.rationale: 'Nice' is subjective and underspecified, leading to materially different expectations for design and content.

evaluations.evidence: results to be stored in a non-identifiable way
evaluations.rationale: 'Non-identifiable' is vague (e.g., anonymization, pseudonymization, aggregation) and can lead to materially different implementations and privacy guarantees.

evaluations.evidence: see some metrics on use of the game
evaluations.rationale: 'Some metrics' is underspecified (which metrics, granularity, timeframes), allowing materially different interpretations of what to show.
